title: Pañcopacāra: worship with five offerings

words.meaning: laṃ, the seed syllable of earth
to the one whose self is earth
fragrance (sandal paste)
I offer
haṃ, the seed syllable of space
to the one whose self is space
flowers
I offer
yaṃ, the seed syllable of air
to the one whose self is air
incense
I cause to smell, I offer to be smelt
raṃ, the seed syllable of fire
to the one whose self is fire
the lamp
I show
vaṃ, the seed syllable of water (nectar)
to the one whose self is nectar
nectar (the food offering)
I present
saṃ, the seed syllable of the whole
to the Self of all
worship with all the attendances
I offer

samasa.meaning: to him whose self is earth

translation.literal: “Laṃ”: to the earth-self I offer fragrance. “Haṃ”: to the space-self I offer flowers. “Yaṃ”: to the air-self I offer incense to smell. “Raṃ”: to the fire-self I show the lamp. “Vaṃ”: to the nectar-self I present nectar. “Saṃ”: to the Self of all I offer worship with every attendance.
translation.readable: Five offerings, each with its seed syllable and element: fragrance for earth, flowers for space, incense for air, the lamp for fire, nectar for water; and with saṃ, every service to the Self of all.

sandhi_exceptions.note: the deity and the offering are said as separate members of the formula; the witness leaves the vowels unjoined (अमृतात्मने अमृतं)

meaning: A short mental worship (pañcopacāra, ‘five attendances’) of the goddess before the japa, in the Mylapore prayoga. Each offering is matched to one of the elements and opened with its seed syllable (bīja): laṃ and fragrance for earth, haṃ and flowers for space, yaṃ and incense for air, raṃ and a lamp for fire, vaṃ and nectar for water; a sixth line with saṃ offers everything to the Self of all.
in_the_rite: Step dhyāna, all three services, after the dhyāna verses and before the japa (the Mylapore prayoga only).

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: The matching of seed syllables, elements and offerings (laṃ earth, haṃ space, yaṃ air, raṃ fire, vaṃ nectar) is as M gives it. S has no pañcopacāra.

flags.text: M writes धूपं आघ्रापयामि with the anusvāra before a vowel; the padaccheda (धूपम् आघ्रापयामि) rejoins into धूपमाघ्रापयामि. Proposed text: यं वाय्वात्मने धूपमाघ्रापयामि.
